state.purpose: Can targets AI coding agents. Explicit contracts, reliable generation, local reasoning, precise diagnostics and safe mechanical edits matter; reduced typing alone does not justify change. There are zero external users and no compatibility obligations. The user says the built-in linter should have warned about unnecessarily convoluted extension/MIME ladders.
state.evidence: Existing ordinary value matches support string literal arms, grouped alternatives with | and exhaustive wildcard _. The original application used long false-branch chains of match ext is ".html", then match ext is ".css", etc.; another chain had two decisions whose conditions each OR several equalities. Direct match ext preserves the original distinct handlers, fallback, evaluation order and error behavior for a single immutable str binding and distinct literal strings. One comparison alone is a normal predicate. The compiler already collects nonblocking warnings with source spans and resolved binding identities, including in recoverable checking.
state.mechanism: Proposed deterministic rule recognizes only fully checked ordinary matches with exactly explicit true/false literal arms; the false arm directly contains another ordinary match. Conditions are string-literal equality or OR of those equalities against the same resolved binding, allowing parentheses and reversed equality operands. No property/index reads, calls, intervening statements, mixed subjects, relational tests or duplicate literal strings qualify. Report once at the first qualifying condition, retaining CLI/editor severity warning. No online model is used for linting. Correctness tests must exercise positive and excluded shapes, maximal-chain deduplication and recovery. No measurements or implementation evidence exists yet.

scope.instructions: Given these exact eligibility constraints, which initial warning threshold best provides actionable agent feedback without treating ordinary logic as complexity?

criteria.two: Warn for two or more consecutive eligible decisions, including the observed two-decision OR-group ladder; each is replaceable by direct string cases.
criteria.three: Warn only at three or more eligible decisions, leaving the observed two-decision grouped ladder silent to reduce short-chain findings.
criteria.none: Add no diagnostic yet; rely on the existing match recipe and postpone any repeated-decision warning despite the reported examples.

delivery.instructions: For an eligible ladder, what initial user-facing remediation is justified by the available evidence and safety goals?

criteria.warning: Emit an advisory with stable code, precise span and a recommendation to match the bound string directly using literal cases, | groups and _ fallback; do not supply automatic edits yet.
criteria.autofix: Implement an automatic rewrite in this round in addition to the warning; prove comment retention, formatting and all branch semantics before offering it.
criteria.error: Reject eligible programs with a hard error requiring the flatter syntax rather than an advisory.
